narr: A cold front and upper low crossed the region during the 13th. Steepening lapse rates with the upper low and increasing shear along the front supported afternoon thunderstorm development across northern and eastern Maine. Some of the thunderstorms became severe...producing large hail and damaging winds. Heavy rains also accompanied some of the storms leading to flash flooding.
ev: Thunderstorms with very heavy rain produced localized flash flooding north of Wellington. Up to 3.50 inches of rain fell in several hours. Multiple gravel roads were washed out or damaged due to the flash flooding.

Thunderstorms producing heavy rain led to flash flooding. Up to 3.50 inches of rain fell over several hours. Garland Road was partially blocked and washed out due to overwhelmed culverts. In addition multiple culverts were washed out on Mill Road along the Garland/Charleston town line. Washouts were also reported on Corinth Road and Fernald Road in Garland...with water across other roads. Water was also reported over Kenduskeag Road and Sawyer Road near the Levant/Kenduskeag town line. Puddledock Road...in the area of Paine Road...was flooded and impassible. A road washout was reported on Bradford Road...between Main Road and Puddledock Road. In Charleston...Harris Road was closed and impassible due to flash flooding.
